'''Zuzanna Stefania Siwy''' (born 1972) is a Polish–American chemist at the [[University of California, Irvine]]. Her research considers synthetic nanopores and their application in ionic devices. She is a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]], [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] and Foundation for Polish Science.

== Early life and education ==
Siwy is from [[Poland]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Siwy Lab: Zuzanna Siwy|url=https://www.physics.uci.edu/~zsiwy/zuzanna.html|access-date=2020-12-28|website=www.physics.uci.edu}}</ref> She studied chemistry at the [[Silesian University of Technology]] in [[Poland]]. She graduated with a master's degree in polymer technology in 1995, before completing a doctorate in chemical sciences in 1997. Siwy was a postdoctoral scholar at the [[University of Florida]].<ref name=":0" />

== Research and career ==
Siwy joined the faculty at the [[University of California, Irvine]] in 2005.  In 2012 she was made Professor of Chemical Physics.  She studies synthetic [[Nanopore|nanopores]], which she looks to use as templates for [[Biomimetics|biomimetic]] channels as well as ionic diodes and transistors.<ref name=":0" />
